REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CERRITOS PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
THURSDAY - AUGUST 1, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Recreation Services Division, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 2nd floor, Cerritos, CA, 90703 during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the Commission after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection at the Recreation Services Division during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to recreation@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1254 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The Commission, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 5.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to recreation@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Recreation Services Division no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the Commission prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Recreation Services Division at (562) 916-1254 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

CITY OF CERRITOS
  MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
  AUGUST1, 2024

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.
2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledgeof Allegiance was led by Whitney High School graduate and recipient of the
  Girl Scout Gold Award, Diana Butt.
3.  Roll Call
  PRESENT:  Commissioner Steve Lin
  Commissioner Pat Patnaik
  Vice Chair Ileana Prado
  Chair Pino Pathak

  ABSENT:  Commissioner Richard Martinez

  All Members of the Parks and Recreation Commission were declared present except
  Commissioner Martinez.

  MOTION: Commissioner Patnaik moved to excuse Commissioner Martinez’s absence.
  Vice Chair Prado seconded the motion, which carried, 4-0, with Commissioner Martinez,
  absent

4.  Presentations
4A.  Presentations

  On behalf of the Parks and Recreation Commission, Chair Pathak recognized
  Employeesof the Month for the RecreationServices Division for April 2024, Niya
  Custer and for June 2024, Alexander Nasario and Senior Center Employees of the
  Quarter, for spring Paul Wood and for winter Desiree Phillips.
5.  Public Comments and Suggestions
  David Pylman talked about an update to the City’s protocol manual; discussed the
  extension of office for specific commissions and upcoming changes in commissions and
  committees .

  Teddy Lloyd reported receiving a letter regarding tape applied to the basketball court
  at SunshineParkfor pickleball,which damagedthe court surface.

  There were no other public comments.
 6.  Consent Calendar

6A.  Approval of Minutes for Thursday, May 2, 2024

  MOTION: Commissioner Patnaik moved to approve the Consent Calendar, as
  presented. Vice Chair Pradoseconded the motion, which carried 4-0, with
  Commissioner Martinez, absent.

7.  New and Old Business

7A.  Reviewand consideration of the potential for the development of policy guidelines for
  a memorial bench program.

  Assistant to the City Manager Ryan Carey presented details of the agenda report.

  Chair Pathak invited public comments.

  Courtney Bankheadthanked the Commission for taking this matter into consideration;
  spoke in support of the program to honor her twin sister, Chelsea Bankhead at her
  favorite park in Cerritos, Friendship Park; discussed her love of the park since they
  were children and requested approval of the program.

  There were no other public comments or written correspondencereceived for this item.

  Discussion followed regarding the need to study this item further and carefully,
  whether the Commission would like to move forward with the establishing a program,
  itemsin the staff report that could serve as a potential policy, other similar requests,
  the need to developcriteria for qualifications and next steps.

  MOTION: Commissioner Patnaik moved to direct staff to proceed with the
  development of policy guidelines for a memorial bench program.

  Discussionfollowed regarding the possibility of tabling the item to allow the
  Commissiontime to study it further and options for the Commissionat this time.
  The motion died for lack of a second.

  ParksSuperintendentTodd I<uhacknowledgedthere is a lot of work that needsto be
  done with this program.

  MOTION: CommissionerPatnaik moved to direct staff to proceedwith the
  development of policy guidelines for a memorial bench program. Vice Chair Prado
  secondedthe motion, which carried 4-0, with Commissioner Martinez, absent.
7B.  Reviewand considerationof an informational review of the Spring Fling and Fireworks
  Spectacular Celebrating the City’s 68th Anniversary held on April 27, 2024.

  Recreation Services Supervisor Jill Toda displayed a PowerPointpresentation with
  details of the agenda report.

  Chair Pathak invited public comments.

  Therewere no public comments or written correspondencereceivedfor this item.

   Discussionfollowed regarding the possibility of inviting community organizations to
  operate game booths.

  MOTION: Vice Chair Pradomoved to receive and file the report. Commissioner
  Patnaik seconded the motion, which carried 4-0, with Commissioner Martinez, absent.

7C.  Reviewand consideration of an information review of the 2024 Women's Day
  Luncheon held at the Cerritos Senior Center.

  Senior Services Supervisor Jesse Zavala displayed a PowerPointpresentation with
  details of the agenda report.

  Chair Pathak invited public comments.

  There were no public comments or written correspondencereceived for this item.

  Discussionfollowed regarding the possibility of fundraising to help fund the event in
  the future,

  MOTION: Commissioner Patnaik moved to receive and file the report. Vice Chair
  Pradoseconded the motion, which carried 4-0, with Commissioner Martinez, absent.

7D.  Reviewand considerationof an information review of the 51stAnnual Let FreedomRing
  Celebration .

  Recreation Services Supervisor Stefanie Linn displayed a PowerPoint presentation with
  details of the Agenda Report.

  Chair Pathak invited public comments.

  Mr. Pylman, a Cerritos resident, suggested reevaluating having community groups
  sponsor food booths for future events.

  There were no other public comments or written correspondencereceivedfor this item.

  Discussionfollowed regarding attendance.

  MOTION: Commissioner Patnaik moved to receive and file the report. Vice Chair
  Pradoseconded the motion, which carried 4-0, with Commissioner Martinez, absent.

8.  Communications

8A.  Reports from Designated Commission Staff Liaison

  Recreation Services Superintendent Sherr6 Titus announced this is the section of the
  agenda where the program reports will be presented moving forward.

  Ms. Toda provided an update on Recreation Services programs, classes and activities.

  Mr. Zavala provided an update on Senior Services programs, classes and activities.

  Discussion followed regarding the S.P.I.C.E. program, reinstating excursions and the
  notary service.

 8B.  Reports from Parks and Recreation Commission Members

  Chair Pathak commented on the possibility of connecting schools with parks by
  establishing a tree-planting program for the schools.

  Ms. Titus noted the new protocolsfor the Commissionto request a report on a
  potential program.

  There was consensusfrom the Commissionto direct staff to return with a memo with
  details about a potential program.

  Chair Pathak welcomed Commissioner Lin to the Commission.

  Vice Chair Prado spoke about attending several City league soccer games and asked
  about the possibility of an implementing a City baseballleague and other programs.
9.  Adjournment
  The meeting was adjourned at 8:30 p.m.
